we have identified and characterized the diversity and persistence in a raw milk cheese of a number of LAB strains, including some that are probably autochthonous to the cheese production environment.

the combined typing approach using (GTG)-PCR fingerprinting and AFLP analysis is a useful tool to evaluate the diversity of lactic acid starter and nonstarter cultures during the production and maturation of artisanal cheeses.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of a polyphasic approach, including (GTG)-PCR fingerprinting and 16S rDNA sequencing, can provide a more comprehensive insight into the diversity of LAB associated with cheese production.
the microbial community of the cheese production environment can be studied in a more detailed way by combining different typing techniques.
the cheese is not a sterile food, and that it is a complex ecosystem.
